outgoing.explanation: The court records establish the person Isacke Gurney but state no parentage, so their bearing on the identification is indirect.

shortLabel: Isacke Gurney court cluster: Scituate 1663/4; Suffolk file 792, 1667

sources.alignmentNote: Two colonial court records of a young Isacke Gurney (Scituate 1663/4; Medford/Boston 1667); neither states parentage. Full treatment on research/people/isaac-gurney-scituate-boston.md.
sources.excerpt: Isacke Gurney, for pilfering and other disorderly liueing, was sentenced by the Court to bee whipt
sources.locator: Plymouth Court Orders 1661–1668 images 35, 37 (arks 3:1:3Q9M-C9BJ-NW1P-1, 3:1:3Q9M-C9BJ-NW15-5); Suffolk County Court Case Files 1666–1668 file no. 792 images 56–59 (arks 3:1:3Q9M-CSVR-R913-N, 3:1:3Q9M-CSVR-R91S-Y)

statement: A young Isacke Gurney appears in a tight cluster of colonial court records — whipped for pilfering at Scituate (Plymouth court, 1 March 1663/4) and jailed for vagrancy and burglary at Medford, committed to the Boston prison under Daniel Gookin's warrant (Suffolk County court file no. 792, June 1667); neither record states his parentage.
